precepts.text: From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. Who are the violent that Christ was talking about? Rome.
precepts.point: You see that last sentence: spacious public spaces for worshippers and pilgrims. Meaning the other nations had a place now; they could come and look at what was going on in the temple. That was not in the original design that God gave us. Herod added it. Herod was an Idumean, an Edomite, and this Edomite wanted favor with the Jews.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Herod the Edomite rebuilt the temple to win favor with the Jews and impress Rome. Christ spoke of what was happening in his day: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.”

Who are the violent Christ was talking about? Rome. Rome took the kingdom by force.

And in the years just before the time of Christ, Judea was controlled by an Edomite faction who usurped the Judahite name, land and heritage. Usurped the name means they became Jewish: we are converts, we are Jews now. That is what Herod was doing. Historically the Edomites became known as Jews, derived from Judea and from Judah, though they were never of Judah or Israel. The violent took the kingdom by force, and then they took the name.

precepts.text: The kingdom of heaven, that's Israel, suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The violent is the Romans; Esau is the Romans. Esau is the violent man, the wicked man.
precepts.point: The Bible calls the evil man, or the violent man, the wicked. Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man, who have purposed to overthrow my goings.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom of heaven, that's Israel, and Israel suffereth violence. The violent that take it by force are the Romans, and Esau is the Romans.

That puts a name on the man of Psalms 140. The Bible calls the evil man, the violent man, the wicked, and Esau is the violent man, the wicked man. “They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips”: they are liars. And they “have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

So David's cry, “preserve me from the violent man”, is Israel's cry to be kept from the hands of Esau, the Romans, who have done violence to the kingdom of heaven from the days of John the Baptist until now.

precepts.text: Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. The subject matter is the kingdom of heaven. From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The kingdom of heaven where the Most High is suffered no violence; the violence was happening to us, in our kingdom. The Romans came into our heaven and took our kingdom by force. That is why the disciples asked in Acts 1:6, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?
precepts.point: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God. The wilderness is Africa; we fled out of Jerusalem into Africa, the same place where Joseph took the young child and his mother. Then a place was prepared, which is the Americas. A thousand two hundred and threescore days: 1260 days, three and a half, the same period written as forty and two months and as a time, times, and the dividing of time in Daniel 7 and 8.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
“And there appeared another wonder in heaven”: in our heaven. Christ explains why it is said that way. “Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.” Nobody was greater than John the Baptist except Christ; he was the forerunner to Christ. So the subject matter at this time is the kingdom of heaven.

“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” What is the kingdom of heaven? The Israelites, the twelve tribes of Israel. The kingdom of heaven where the Most High is suffered no violence. The violence was happening to us, in our kingdom.

That is the great red dragon. The Romans are the red people that came into our heaven and took our kingdom by force. That is why the disciples asked in Acts 1:6 whether he would at that time restore again the kingdom to Israel: the Romans had taken our heaven by force.

So when Revelation says a great red dragon appeared “in heaven”, it means he came into our rulership, the kingdom of Israel, and took it by violence.

precepts.text: And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve. The rest Christ offers is rest from the sorrow, the fear, and the hard bondage of Israel's captivity. That is who come unto me is addressed to.
precepts.point: A critic was played mocking the Israelites, quoting: come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest, as if it were addressed to everybody. Here is the precept he does not know.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
A critic was played mocking the Israelites, quoting “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest” as if Christ said it to everybody: come unto me all ye, not you that accept that I'm black. That is what Edom is doing now, hiring black people, dumb Africans, to use Zionist talking points against the truth. We didn't say it; a black man said it. So here is the precept he does not know.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” Rest from what? From thy sorrow. From thy fear. From the hard bondage: that's slavery. Wherein thou wast made to serve. The man on the screen don't know what the hell he's talking about.

The rest Christ promises the labouring and heavy laden is rest from the sorrow, the fear and the hard bondage of Israel's captivity. The ones heavy laden are the people who were made to serve. That is who “come unto me” is addressed to.

Isaiah opens the chapter by saying who gets that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel.” We are messed up as a people, not in our right minds yet, but because of the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob he will yet choose us. That's mercy, and we need that mercy.

precepts.point: The bottle says you are alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. The bottle starts talking to you like it is scripture: drink me and I will take away thy sorrows, I am the comfort of them all. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
The bottle says, forget your pain; the Bible says, “Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.” The bottle says, numb your sorrow. Christ answers that lie: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”

The bottle offers to carry your burden for you. It talks to you like scripture in a dark room with one light over the table: drink me, I can take away thy sorrows; you're depressed, don't worry about it; you're stressed out, put the kids to bed early and drink me. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

Christ is the one who actually takes the weight. The labouring and heavy laden are told to come to him, not to the liquor store, and he gives rest. The bottle only numbs the sorrow until tomorrow; casting the burden on the Lord is how he sustains you and keeps the righteous from being moved.

precepts.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Heavy laden with sin, and the rest is not a good night's sleep: it is the kingdom, rulership for a thousand years under Christ. This is why we need a saviour; we cannot do it without Christ.
precepts.point: They have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward. That is why we went into captivity: Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 laid out the curses for breaking the commandments, and many of us are still moonwalking away from the Most High. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Isaiah calls us “a people laden with iniquity.” Christ answers that very word: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” Heavy laden with what? With sin, the iniquity Isaiah just named.

That is why we are in need of a saviour. We read the history of our forefathers in the wilderness: the Most High showed great signs and wonders, and we were still a stiff-necked, hard-headed people. We are “a sinful nation”, “a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters.” We forsake the Lord every time we sin, and we have “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger.” That is why the so-called blacks and Hispanics went into captivity, just as Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 laid out the curses for breaking the commandments. Many of our brothers and sisters are still going backward, moonwalking away from the Most High. Brothers and sisters, we cannot do it without Christ.

So be honest and sincere, even in prayer. Do not go to the Most High acting righteous when you are full of dead bones, sin and guile. None of us is righteous; we are trying, but there is sin still in us. Open your mouth and confess the things you are battling with.

“and I will give you rest.” That rest is not a good night’s sleep. It is our land, the kingdom of God, rulership for a thousand years under Christ. That is the true rest he is talking about, but we have to come unto him. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent.

precepts.text: Solomon sat upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel: Israel is the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: The kingdom of heaven that suffers violence is the nation of Israel, the kingdom of the Lord Solomon sat over, and the violent who take it by force were Rome, the same violent man of Psalms 140 and the same man today. What would Jesus say? He called them the violent.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
How is the kingdom of heaven suffering violence? Is somebody jumping up in the sky punching God in the face? No. David answers it: “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” Israel is called the kingdom of the Lord. The throne Solomon sat on was over a nation of people on the earth.

So when Christ says “from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence”, the kingdom of heaven is the nation of Israel. It is our people who suffered the violence.

“and the violent take it by force”. That is Rome. The violent man Christ speaks of is the same one just read in Psalms 140: “preserve me from the violent man; Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” They sharpen their tongues like a serpent, and “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their media, their philosophies, their religions, their politics. They have “purposed to overthrow my goings”, and the one whose goings they overthrow is the Israelites.

It is the same man being violent to us today. So what would Jesus say? He already spoke on it: Christ called Rome the violent man. They are the violent, and the kingdom they take by force is Israel.

precepts.text: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they said, Behold a winebibber; yet he never was drunken.
precepts.point: His eyes shall be red with wine: Christ drank wine, so much that men called him a winebibber, but he was never drunken.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.” Christ drank wine, so much that men called him a winebibber. But he was never drunken.

That is “His eyes shall be red with wine.” Jacob saw Christ of the tribe of Judah eating and drinking, and the accusation of the Pharisees confirms it.

precepts.text: No man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
precepts.point: No one knows the Father until Christ reveals him, because Christ is the mediator. That is why our brothers and sisters caught up in Christianity and Islam do not know the Most High: he has not been revealed to them, and they have not been shown who they are. The word comes down in order, from the Most High to Christ, to the angels, and into our spirit when it is time to wake up; the Most High does not deal with us directly right now, because we are too full of sin.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.”

No one knows the Father until Christ reveals him, because Christ is the mediator. That is why Samuel, though he ran to Eli, saying “Here am I”, “did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him.”

And that is why our brothers and sisters caught up in Christianity and Islam do not know the Most High: he has not been revealed to them, and they have not been shown who they are.

precepts.text: The kingdom of heaven suffereth violence and the violent take it by force; the violent men of that time were Rome fighting against the kingdom, which is Israel.
precepts.point: He delivers David from his enemies and lifts him above those that rise against him, delivering him from the violent man. The enemies are not just going to and fro; there is a people who serve satan, the so-called white man, to make it plain.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“thou hast delivered me from the violent man.” Christ speaks of that violence: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.”

The kingdom of heaven suffered violence, and the violent men of that time were Rome, fighting against the kingdom, which is Israel. The enemies are not just going to and fro; there is a people who serve satan, the so-called white man, to make it plain. Those are the violent that David is delivered from when the Most High lifts him up above those that rise up against him.

precepts.text: From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence and the violent take it by force.
precepts.point: The kingdom of heaven, the Israelites, suffered violence and the violent took it by force; Israel was taken out of the land by violence and Jerusalem is trodden down of the Gentiles until their time is fulfilled.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion”. Christ says what happened to it: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.”

The kingdom of heaven is the Israelites, and it suffered violence; the violent took it by force. Israel was taken out of the land by violence, the same violence Micah speaks of, coveting fields and taking them by violence. The city of the great King, beautiful for situation, was seized by the violent.

precepts.text: The kingdom of heaven suffers violence and the violent take it by force; the nations have taken it by the sword.
precepts.point: A heart that devises wicked imaginations such as sex changes, homosexuality and lesbianism; feet swift running to mischief such as gangs and gang initiation; a false witness that speaks lies; and he that sows discord among brethren through gossip and heresies.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
The Lord hates “hands that shed innocent blood”. Christ says: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom of heaven suffers violence and the violent take it by force; the nations have taken it by the sword.

The hands that took the kingdom by force are hands that shed innocent blood. Because the Most High hates those hands, the murderers among Esau and the nations that took us captive and shed our blood have no place ruling over us in the kingdom, yet our people keep trying to get them in.

precepts.text: Blessed is he whosoever shall not be offended in me.
precepts.point: There is a difference in offense. If you offend a brother or cause harm, make it right; but if you bring out God's commandments, such as a sister wearing what belongs to a man or a brother refusing to grow his beard, and they are offended, then they are offended at Christ, not at you.

note.label: Proverbs 18: The Power of the Tongue and Righteous Judgment

precepts.why:
There is a difference in offense. If you offend a brother or cause harm, make it right. But if you bring out God’s commandments, such as a sister wearing what belongs to a man or a brother refusing to grow his beard, and they are offended, then they are offended at Christ, not at you.

“And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.” The one offended at the commandment is offended in Christ, and the blessing is on the one who is not.

precepts.text: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped, and the tongue of the dumb sing.
precepts.point: Christ answers by pointing to the works: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. He is quoting Isaiah back to them.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

precepts.why:
John sends to ask if he is the one, and Christ answers by pointing to the works: “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.” He is quoting Isaiah back to them.

Isaiah: “Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you. Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing”. The blind seeing, the deaf hearing, the lame leaping: these are the signs Isaiah gave of the day your God comes to save you. John knew the prophet, so the answer told him what he asked: the works Isaiah wrote of are being done, and the one Isaiah wrote of is here.

precepts.text: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me; and he is like a refiner's fire.
precepts.point: John is the messenger written of, sent before the face of the Lord to prepare the way.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

precepts.why:
“What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?” Not a reed shaken with the wind, nor a man in soft clothing, for “they that wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses”, but a prophet, “and more than a prophet. For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.”

The writing is Malachi: “Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in”. John is that messenger, sent before the face of the Lord to prepare the way, and the Lord who comes suddenly to his temple behind him is Christ.

Malachi goes on: “But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner’s fire, and like fullers’ soap: And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness.” The one the messenger prepares the way for is a refiner's fire; he purifies and purges. That is what came behind John, and it is why John was more than a prophet.

precepts.text: Solomon sat upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel, which is what the kingdom is.
precepts.point: The kingdom in view is Israel. The violence is what was done to them, and it is seen plainly in what the Romans did to Jerusalem, taking the kingdom by bloodshed.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

precepts.why:
“from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom in view is Israel.

David shows what the kingdom is: “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” The throne Solomon sat on is the throne of the kingdom of the Lord, and that kingdom is over Israel. The kingdom of the Lord and the kingdom of Israel are one and the same.

So the violence the kingdom of heaven suffers is what was done to Israel. It is seen plainly in what the Romans did to Jerusalem, taking the kingdom by bloodshed. The violent took it by force.

precepts.text: I will send you Elijah the prophet, and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children.
precepts.point: All the prophets and the law prophesied until John, and if ye will receive it, this is Elias which was for to come.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

precepts.why:
“For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.” Elias was for to come; that is a prophecy, and it is Malachi's.

“Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.” Elijah the prophet is sent before the day of the Lord to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children and the children to their fathers. John came before Christ doing that work, so Christ says, if you will receive it, this is Elias. The law and the prophets prophesied until John because John is where the prophecy of Elijah's coming was met.

precepts.text: John sent from prison to ask, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another; he too expected deliverance at that time.
precepts.point: "Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?”

The disciples asked about restoring the kingdom because they thought Rome was the last captivity. John the Baptist thought the same. He sent from prison to ask whether Christ was the one, because he too expected deliverance at that time.

precepts.text: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, and the poor have the gospel preached unto them, so freely as we received, we give them the gospel.
precepts.point: We cannot heal a body today, but we heal every day with the word: drug dealers, baby mothers, and survivors of mental, physical, alcoholic, drug, and religious abuse are healed when they receive the truth. When people say we do not feed the poor, the truth is the poor have the gospel preached to them, and that is the healing.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Christ described his work this way: “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.” The lame walking at the temple gate is that work carried on by Peter, and everything the apostles did was prepared and taught to them; they did not move independently.

We cannot heal a body today, but the last thing on that list is ours: the poor have the gospel preached to them. When people say we do not feed the poor, the truth is that the poor have the gospel preached to them, and that is the healing. Freely as we received, we give them the gospel.

precepts.text: "The kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force," and the violent were Esau ruling through Rome, who stole it by force.
precepts.point: The kingdom itself was taken by force, and Israel was led away captive into all nations, showing again that our people are the ones who lost it and must have it restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The kingdom itself was stolen: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.”

The violent were Esau ruling through Rome. They took the kingdom by force, and what is taken by force has to be restored to its proper owner. That is the restitution: the kingdom restored again to Israel.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why:
Here's another one, with John the Baptist. And anybody that thinks John the Baptist was a wicked negro, you're on crack. “Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?” Why'd he ask that? John was in prison. He thought deliverance was at that time. That's why he was talking greasy to Herod: remember Herod walked in with his brother's wife and John was bold, it's unlawful for you to have your brother's wife, and they arrested him and put him in jail. So he's thinking, I'm good, Christ is going to deliver me out of here. But that wasn't the time.

“Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:” To encourage John. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.” Here it comes. “And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.” He was telling John, don't be offended, because this is not the time for deliverance. This is the time for me to be sacrificed. Everybody thought it was going to be the same thing; nobody wanted to hear the sacrifice stuff. All Israel wanted the deliverance part, the vengeance part, but that was not the time.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why:
This goes for brothers out there saying John the Baptist was wicked. John the Baptist by this time had gotten killed already, but now Christ knew his crucifixion was coming, and look what happened. Remember John is dead already.

“And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart, And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.” Watch this. “And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.” So John the Baptist was talking to Christ with Moses. How you going to read that and go, "Oh, he was wicked"? You are stupid as hell; something's wrong with you. John got killed already, and now in the spirit realm the disciples saw Christ speaking with Moses and John the Baptist, Elijah. You can't make this stuff up.

points: From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The kingdom of heaven here is the children of Israel; we are the kingdom of heaven. The violent at that time were the Romans, and the violent have taken the kingdom by force.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: A critic was played mocking the Israelites, quoting: come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest, as if it were addressed to everybody. Here is the precept he does not know.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

points: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me. Many come to this truth and leave offended, whatever camp they joined. But leaving a group does not change what you are biologically. Saying, I used to be an Israelite, is like saying, I used to be Chinese. You will always be what you were born; renouncing it only means you are lost to your people and your God.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: The kingdom of heaven that suffers violence is the nation of Israel, the kingdom of the Lord Solomon sat over, and the violent who take it by force were Rome, the same violent man of Psalms 140 and the same man today. What would Jesus say? He called them the violent.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

points: From the days of John the Baptist the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.
They took it by breaking the family: separating the woman from her husband and removing his comfort, strength and reverence.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

points: John hears in the prison the works of Christ and sends two of his disciples to ask, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Christ answers by pointing to the works: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. He is quoting Isaiah back to them.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: What went ye out into the wilderness to see? Not a reed shaken with the wind, nor a man in soft clothing, but a prophet, and more than a prophet.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: John is the messenger written of, sent before the face of the Lord to prepare the way.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist, notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.
The kingdom in view is Israel. The violence is what was done to them, and it is seen plainly in what the Romans did to Jerusalem, taking the kingdom by bloodshed.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: All the prophets and the law prophesied until John, and if ye will receive it, this is Elias which was for to come.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: That generation is likened to children in the markets who piped and were not danced to. Christ did not move to the beat of their drum.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: John came neither eating nor drinking and they said he hath a devil; the Son of man came eating and drinking and they called him a gluttonous man. Nothing would have satisfied them.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Woe unto Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum, because the mighty works were done among them and they repented not.
Tyre, Sidon and Sodom would have repented at what these cities saw. Men watched works no ordinary man could do and still would not turn.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: These things are hid from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. No man knoweth the Father save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Read above verse 14 so we know the context. “Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist:” Christ said there's nobody greater than John the Baptist. “notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.” Why? Because in the kingdom of heaven, when you read Isaiah, all Israel shall be all righteous: no fears, no more sin. That's why the least in the kingdom is going to be greater than John was at that time.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence,” By Rome, at the hands of Rome. “and the violent take it by force.” How did Rome get over Jerusalem? Around 63 BC General Pompey came in with a whole military and took Jerusalem, took the land of Israel. That's how Rome got their foothold on the land, so that's why when Christ was born they all had to pay taxes to Caesar.

The violence wasn't up in the sky. The violence was to the kingdom of heaven on earth, letting you know that we are the kingdom of heaven. The violent: he's calling Rome the violent. The white man is the violent man.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: “For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.” So Christ revealed that John the Baptist was who? Elijah. This goes for brothers out there saying John the Baptist was wicked; Matthew 17 settles it.
